[[File:DecipherCon 2000 banner.gif|center|640px]]
[[File:Doubletree Resort Kissimmee aerial.jpg|thumb|right|320px|The Doubletree Resort, Kissimmee. Photo: USGS.]]
'''DecipherCon 2000''' was Decipher's second company convention, held 5–8 October 2000 at the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, 3011 Maingate Lane, Kissimmee, Florida. It hosted the [[2000 Decipher World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]], in which [[Matt Sokol]] defeated [[Yannick Lapointe]].<ref name="sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (Wayback 9 October 2006)</ref><ref name="jls3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001117011300/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/jls3.html Matt Sokol, 2000 Star Wars CCG World Champion!], Jean-Luc Simard, Decipher (Wayback 17 November 2000)</ref><ref name="addr">[https://www.travelweekly.com/Hotels/Kissimmee-FL/Holiday-Inn-Resort-by-the-Parks-p60120676 Holiday Inn Resort by the Parks], Travel Weekly (3011 Maingate Lane, Kissimmee, FL 34747; telephone 407-396-1400)</ref>

The 1999 convention had been in Virginia Beach ([[DecipherCon 1999]]). Decipher billed 2000 as "the Whole Shebang": World Championship play, first looks at new product, and seminars inside product development.<ref name="home">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040217015645/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ DecipherCon 2000], Decipher (Wayback 17 February 2004)</ref><ref name="tfn">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Decipher_Update_DecipherCon_2000_75291.asp Decipher Update: DecipherCon 2000], TheForce.net (5 September 2000)</ref>

== Venue and dates ==

* '''Dates:''' 5–8 October 2000 (Thursday–Sunday)
* '''Site:''' Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, 3011 Maingate Lane, Kissimmee, Florida<ref name="sched" /><ref name="addr" />
* '''Master of ceremonies:''' [[Mark Tuttle]], Decipher net representative<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="insider">''Star Wars Insider'' 52 (2000), "It's a CCG TKO When Star Wars Fans Compete at DecipherCon 2000"</ref>

The hotel is two seven-story towers joined by a lobby, about a mile from the Walt Disney World entrance. The same building later operated as Holiday Inn Resort Kissimmee by the Parks.<ref name="addr" />

World Championship constructed days ran Thursday through Saturday. Sunday held the team constructed event and remaining side tournaments.<ref name="sched" /><ref name="events">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081013224103/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/events.html DecipherCon master tournament schedule], Decipher (Wayback 13 October 2008)</ref>

A false fire alarm at 7 a.m. on Friday 6 October emptied the hotel. [[Maarten Logghe]] was in the parking lot when staff called it a false alarm.<ref name="loftus">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050318081253/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/rl1.html FIRE ALARM], Rich Loftus, Decipher (Wayback 18 March 2005)</ref>

== Guests ==

Special guests were [[Michonne Bourriague]] (Aurra Sing) and [[Shannon Baksa]] (Mara Jade). Both sat autograph tables during the weekend.<ref name="home" /><ref name="tfn" />

Saturday 7 October at 1 p.m. [[Tom Lischke]] held a Star Wars CCG question-and-answer session, including the upcoming [[Shadows of the Empire]] expansion. Friday's program included a card-production seminar and a Digital Deck demonstration.<ref name="seminars">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061114195529/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/seminars/ DecipherCon 2000 seminars], Decipher (Wayback 14 November 2006)</ref><ref name="loftus" /><ref name="tfn" />

The first annual Decipher Olympics held sorting competitions, card-house building, and card tosses. One card toss sent a card the length of the hall into a chandelier.<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="hickey">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ mr-hickey-goes-to-florida], Charles "Teacher" Hickey, Decktech (14 October 2000)</ref>

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

Full results, lists, decks, and the Final Confrontation are on [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]. The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Death Star II]]. [[Justin Pakes]] directed the Star Wars rooms. Sokol (United States) defeated Lapointe (Canada).<ref name="home" /><ref name="jls3" /><ref name="tennet">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cards], Alex "Greedo" Tennet, Decktech (13 October 2000)</ref>

Day 1 had 72 players. Sokol finished 36th, then advanced through Day 2 and Day 3. Twelve players reached Day 3. Lapointe led that table 8 (+47). Sokol 6 (+23) took the second Final Confrontation seat.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="insider" /><ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010303120030/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars3.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 3], Decipher (Wayback 3 March 2001)</ref><ref name="sokol-trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref>

Day 1 started hours late. Sokol wrote that the open began about 1 p.m., three hours after the posted time.<ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref> [[John Arendt]] waited three hours past the published start.<ref name="arendt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2], John Arendt, Decktech (9 October 2000)</ref> [[Hayes Hunter]] later said first pairings went up at 1 p.m. when play was supposed to start in the morning, and the day ran until 2 a.m.<ref name="hayes-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2794s SWCCG PDS2: Hayes Hunter Worlds 2023 Champion Interview], BillBisco2 (10 May 2025), 46:34–46:54. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-qJuistFFk9M Internet Archive]; [https://web.archive.org/web/20261016010406/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M watch-page snapshot] (Wayback 16 October 2026).</ref> [[Charlie Herren]] called Day 1 the most poorly run tournament he had seen.<ref name="herren">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercond1322/ the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercon], Charlie Herren, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref> [[Paul Todd Feldman]] said the tournament software was not working properly and that pairings took a long time.<ref name="feldman-pds2-ops">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=2428s SWCCG PDS2: Paul Todd Feldman Interview], BillBisco2 (29 May 2025), 40:28–40:37. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-b9f9tNBiU2I Internet Archive].</ref>

Thursday's first [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] product tournament drew 24 players in a side hall while Worlds Day 1 ran next door. Light Side dominated (Lapointe was the only Dark winner after game 1). [[Koen Meijssen]] (Holland) 8 (+69) beat [[Martin Akesson]] (Sweden) 6 (+17) in the final by 3 Force. [[Jeff Weitkamp]] (Gold 40) was tournament director.<ref name="fkl2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher (Wayback 7 January 2001)</ref>

== Star Wars CCG Team Championship ==

Sunday 8 October 2000 was the DecipherCon constructed team event. [[Team Albany]] won with a four-player team: [[Matt Sokol]], [[Jonny Chu]], [[Chris Terwilliger]], and [[Brian Terwilliger]].<ref name="eltwigg">[https://x.com/eltwigg/status/1327604566830043142 Brian Terwilliger], X (14 November 2020)</ref><ref name="sokol-trando" />

== Other games ==

The same weekend held World Championships for ''Star Trek'' CCG (Eric Johnfauno over Brian Sykes) and Young Jedi (Ian Vincent over Philippe Parise), plus more than 60 side tournaments.<ref name="home" /><ref name="insider" /> Saturday night's Great Tribble Hunt was a scheduled ''Star Trek'' side event.<ref name="events" />

=== Hallway gaming ===

On 5 October 2025 [[Kevin Reitzel]] posted stills from Brandon Baity's YouTube video "DecipherCon 2000 - Post Con Hallway Gaming." He asked the community to help tag the players.<ref name="fb-hall">[https://www.facebook.com/kevin.reitzel/posts/deciphercon-2000-25-years-ago-screen-shots-from-the-youtube-video-deciphercon-20/10237436825557579/ DecipherCon 2000, 25 years ago], Kevin Reitzel, Facebook (5 October 2025)</ref> [[Jim Colson]] is in that video.

== Trip reports ==

Official Decipher "Zoom In" copy came from Francis K. Lalumiere, Jean-Luc Simard, Marcus Sheppard, and John Kaufeld. The Star Wars pieces are Lalumiere's Jabba's Palace Sealed report and Simard's Final Confrontation report.<ref name="reports">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001116233700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/index.html DecipherCon 2000 reports], Decipher (Wayback 16 November 2000)</ref> Rich Loftus wrote the Friday fire-alarm floor report.<ref name="loftus" />

Player reports went up on Decktech within days. They describe the late Day 1 start, deck-check disqualifications, and the Final Confrontation:

* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ Matt Sokol] — all three Worlds days, [[Team Albany]], the missing Luke, and the Final Confrontation
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-world-day-3-whos-the-man-not-med1324/ Yannick Lapointe] — Day 3 table, Super Falcon vs Sokol, and the Final Confrontation
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ Alex Tennet] — UK travel, [[Team OK-UK]] shirts, Day 1 games, DQs, and watching the final
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ Charles Hickey] — Endor crew, card toss, Day 1 games
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-the-bad-player-goes-to-deciphercond1322/ Charlie Herren] — Day 1 wait, pickup games, "most poorly run tourney I have ever seen"
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-09-deciphercon-beedos-report-day-1-2d1314/ John Arendt] — three-hour wait past the posted start
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], Trandosite, 25 October 2000 (Rod Latham / Alex Tennet)
* Decktech also carried reports from [[Dominic Gaudreault]], [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Bastian Winkelhaus]], Doug Faust, [[Martin Akesson]], [[Mike Kessling]], Tim Guzman, and others, indexed from [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/tournament_reports/ the tournament-reports list] under 8–15 October 2000

Later interviews returned to the same weekend:

* [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJuistFFk9M&t=2794s Hayes Hunter] — Day 1 pairings at 1 p.m. and play until 2 a.m.
* [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b9f9tNBiU2I&t=2428s Paul Todd Feldman] — tournament software and slow pairings
* [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jFXqTc1jkNc Matt Sokol] looking back at the match and [[Team Albany]]
